text: ← Advanced contents AVAILABLE CHAPTERS WHAT YOU WILL LEARNDerive a diffusion clock from charge–neutral drift and check strong-coupling and small-drift assumptions. Connect to foundations: Stars, gas, vacuum, and the forces of nature ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Neutrals do not directly feel the magnetic force Most particles in a molecular cloud are neutral. A small charged component couples to the magnetic field and transfers momentum to neutrals through collisions. Different velocities allow magnetic flux to move relative to neutral material. Here ambipolar diffusion specifically means this ion–neutral drift in a weakly ionized astrophysical gas. Assume charges are sufficiently tied to the field and neglect ion inertia. This model does not solve charge separation. Omit Ohmic resistance, Hall effects, and a distribution of charged dust grains. 02Balance magnetic force against drag Let vD = vᵢ−vₙ. Drag on the ions is −γρᵢρₙvD. Balancing it against the Lorentz force determines the drift. Use Gaussian CGS units below: densities in g cm⁻³ and field strength in gauss. The drag coefficient is a supplied material input with dimensions, not a dimensionless efficiency. γρᵢρₙvD ≈ (∇×B)×B4π ηAD=B²4πγρᵢρₙ, tAD∼L²ηAD ηAD has units cm²/s and is a magnetic diffusivity, rather than an electrical resistance. At fixed number ionization fraction, increasing gas density strengthens drag and slows the relaxation of a fixed field pattern. A stronger field increases the magnetic force as well as the diffusivity. 03A single Fourier mode makes diffusion solvable Prescribe a static, uniform neutral background and a z-directed field varying weakly along x. Linearize about B₀ and hold ηAD at its background value. Define L = 1/k and wavelength λ = 2πL; using the wavelength in place of L would introduce a factor of 4π² in the decay clock. ∂δB∂t=ηAD∂²δB∂x² BzB₀=1+ε cos(x/L)e−t/tAD, tAD=L²ηAD Charges and field drift away from magnetic maxima toward minima, flattening the pattern. Set ε = 0.1. The neutral background is externally prescribed, so this is a diffusion benchmark, not a self-consistent collapsing cloud. Terms beyond linear order in ε are omitted. vD,x≈εηADLsin(x/L)e−t/tAD 04Compare field smoothing with a gravitational clock Inputs are neutral-particle number density nₙ and number ratio χᵢ = nᵢ/nₙ, not an ion mass fraction. Set ρₙ = 2.33mₚnₙ and ρᵢ = 29mₚχᵢnₙ for a representative molecular ion. Supply γ = 3.5 × 10¹³ cm³ g⁻¹ s⁻¹, B₀ = 30 μG, and T = 10 K. These composition-dependent choices are illustrative inputs, not universal constants. tff=√3π32Gρₙ, tin=1γρₙ, tni=1γρᵢ Borrow the free-fall time of a uniform sphere at the same density solely as a gravitational clock. tᵢₙ measures ion momentum adjustment to neutrals; tₙᵢ measures neutral adjustment to ions. Neglecting ion inertia requires tᵢₙ to be short relative to field evolution. Strong coupling does not require exactly zero drift. 05Dissipation and limits of the approximation The wavelength-averaged perturbation energy is ε²B₀² exp(−2t/tAD)/(16π). Its loss rate equals the averaged drag heating γρᵢρₙ⟨vD²⟩ to the retained order. This provides an energy check. Dissipated energy would heat matter, although the panel does not evolve temperature or neutral motion. The constant low-drift coefficient also assumes drift well below particle thermal speeds. Inspect vD,max/cₛ and tᵢₙ/tAD. Large values signal that interpreting the fixed-coefficient result physically requires more care. Sound speed is a thermal-speed proxy here, and the displayed flag is a heuristic validity check, not a sharp stability threshold. Compare with ideal MHD in MRI and the unmagnetized isothermal filament. This identifies where flux freezing enters an argument. A short diffusion time alone does not prove that a cloud must form a star; forces, geometry, and boundary conditions still matter. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. At fixed density, ionization, and field, double the perturbation scale L. How do diffusion time and initial drift speed change? Show the answer and reasoning With fixed η, tAD = L²/η grows fourfold and vD,max = εη/L halves at fixed fractional amplitude ε. L is 1/k, not the wavelength.
